subject: Streaming concurrency limiter causing truncated responses - Hydra Health
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: hydra-support@hydrahealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming concurrency limiter causing truncated responses - Hydra Health

Hi Aditi / Hydra team,

We're seeing a spike in truncated streaming responses (partial payloads followed by 502) for some long-lived streaming sessions tied to your account. We opened an incident and posted a short notice on the status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-10-07-stream-concurrency.

What we see so far:
- Window: 08:40–09:05 PDT (initial surge) but intermittent through the morning.
- Symptom: client streaming sessions terminate after 40–120s with a 502 and partial output.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate/stream (long-prompt flows).
- Impact: elevated p99 and a handful of active customers (you reported failures).

Immediate mitigation: we temporarily tightened the streaming concurrency limiter to prevent system-wide instability while we investigate. That may increase truncations for long streams — I want to be transparent about the tradeoff.

Attachments: [Attachment: incident_graph.png (image/png)] — shows the truncated response count vs in-flight streams.

Could you share 1–2 example request IDs where you saw truncation? That will speed root cause. We have Marissa and Ben on the thread to coordinate a fix and a brief customer-facing update.

We’ll follow up with a targeted mitigation and timeline by 12:30 PDT. Apologies for the interruption — we know streaming reliability matters to your integration.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
(Attachment: incident_graph.png)

Thanks Vanessa — we saw the same. Example request IDs: hh-req-2026-10-07-3312 and hh-req-2026-10-07-3389. Both are from our real-time transcript flow where sessions run 90–150 seconds.

Attached are excerpts from our client logs showing the 502 arrival immediately after a partial chunk. We rely on long sessions for verbatim transcription, so truncation causes dropped content for our downstream pipeline.

We appreciate the quick note and the status link. Can you confirm whether our SLA/credits will be considered for this window? Also please tell us the expected ETA for a definitive fix — we may toggle some internal retries in the meantime.

— Aditi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 12:20:45 -0700
Subject: RE: Streaming concurrency limiter causing truncated responses - Hydra Health

Hi Aditi — thanks for the request IDs, those are helpful. Quick technical update from the ops team:

Root cause hypothesis (interim):
- A regression in the streaming concurrency estimator caused long-lived streams to be treated as short-lived during an internal rebalancing window. The estimator briefly under-counted active tokens for some connections which let the limiter evict in-flight streams prematurely.
- The tightened limiter we applied as a protective action reduced system-wide risk but increased truncations for the exact long sessions you run.

What we did:
- Deployed a targeted fix to the estimator at 11:50 PDT (small config + logic correction).
- Gradually rolled the fix across the cluster (canaries + 10% / 30% / 100% over 20m).
- Reversed the emergency tightening after the canary looked stable at 12:05 PDT.

Preliminary results: we see a 78% reduction in truncation counts in the next 30 minutes post-rollout (chart attached). We're continuing to monitor for any regressions.

Next steps for you:
- Would you be willing to validate a few previously failing request IDs now (we believe hh-req-2026-10-07-3312 should succeed)?
- We'll produce a short postmortem doc and schedule a 30-min wrap-up call for Thursday to go over root cause, follow-up fixes, and credit eligibility.

Attachments: [Attachment: ops_runbook_v3.md] — internal runbook reference (safe to share redacted).

Apologies for the disruption — we own this and will follow up with a full RCA.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
(marissa.cole@redwood.ai)
